title: UppASD benchmark raw sample record (v1)
description: One executable measurement of one UppASD production run. A raw sample record is never aggregated in place: statistics over several samples live in benchmark_aggregate.v1.schema.json. See benchmarks/README.md and benchmarks/TERMINOLOGY.md for the meaning of case/variant/size/build/run configuration/sample/campaign.

precision_value.description: SINGLE/DOUBLE/MIXED where established by audit; UNKNOWN where not yet audited; null where not applicable (e.g. GPU precision of a CPU-only run).

schema_version.description: Semantic version of this result contract. The v1 schema accepts any 1.x record; a breaking change bumps the major version and adds a new schema file.

record_kind.description: Discriminator. Raw sample records are always individual; aggregation happens in a separate record kind.

run_id.description: Globally unique identifier of this single executable measurement.

variant_id.description: Alternative physics/runtime configuration of the same case, e.g. T0 or finiteT.

size_id.description: Legal geometric replication of the case, e.g. 32x32x32.

sample_index.description: 0-based index of this sample within its (campaign, case, variant, size, build, run configuration) cell.

machine_id.description: Stable identifier of the physical machine. Results from different machines must never be pooled silently.

timestamp_utc.description: UTC start time of the measured process, ISO 8601.

workflow.description: Production workflow under test. ADAPTIVE_CG is reserved and obeys exactly the same headline timing contract as ORDINARY_ASD.

workload_class.description: Which workload-size normalization applies. Neighbour-interaction throughput must not be applied blindly to FFT workloads.

natom.description: Total number of atoms/spins actually simulated.

directed_interactions.description: Total number of directed neighbour interactions (each i->j counted once). null only for pure FFT/dipole workloads.

median_neighbors.description: Optional; recorded where inexpensive to obtain.

fft_grid.description: Physical dipole/FFT grid dimensions [nx, ny, nz]. null for non-FFT workloads.

fft_grid_padded.description: Grid dimensions actually transformed after padding/grid expansion, when they differ from fft_grid; otherwise null.

fft_grid_points.description: Total number of points of the grid actually transformed (product of fft_grid_padded when padded, else of fft_grid).

dipole_backend.description: Dipole implementation actually used, e.g. FFT_FFTW, FFT_CUFFT, MACROCELL, BRUTE_FORCE. null when the case has no dipole term.

backend.description: Execution backend of the production run. CPU means shared-memory CPU/OpenMP.

gpu_backend.description: GPU programming model. HIP is representable here whether or not it has been measured; no HIP performance claim may be made without real hardware execution.

omp_threads.description: Value of OMP_NUM_THREADS actually in force.

omp_places.description: Raw OMP_PLACES value, or null when unset in the environment.

omp_proc_bind.description: Raw OMP_PROC_BIND value, or null when unset in the environment.

omp_dynamic.description: Effective OMP_DYNAMIC state, or null when it could not be determined.

process_affinity.description: Observed CPU affinity mask/list of the benchmark process. null sets the cpu_affinity_unknown quality flag.

requested_precision.description: Precision requested by the build configuration. MIXED is deliberately not implemented in production and must be recorded with precision_support_state = unsupported.

effective_cpu_precision.description: Precision the CPU numerical path actually uses, as established by source/build audit -- not inferred from CMake option names.

effective_gpu_precision.description: Precision the GPU numerical path actually uses, as established by source/build audit. May legitimately differ from effective_cpu_precision for the same requested_precision.

precision_support_state.description: Whether the requested precision is a supported production mode. 'unsupported' is a first-class state (used for MIXED) and is not a generic failed build.

comparison_precision_class.description: How this record may be used in a cross-backend comparison. PRECISION_MATCHED requires audited, genuinely corresponding CPU and GPU precision; PRODUCTION_CONFIGURATION covers real supported modes that are not precision-matched (e.g. CPU double vs CUDA single).

git_commit.description: Full 40-character commit hash of the source the binary was built from.

git_dirty_files.description: Tracked files modified at build time. Empty array when git_dirty is false.

cmake_options.description: CMake cache options relevant to the build, as a name -> value map.

binary_checksum.description: SHA-256 of the executable actually run.

build_id.description: Identifier of the immutable build record this run used.

cpu_physical_cores.description: Total physical cores in the machine.

cpu_threads.description: Total hardware threads in the machine. Greater than cpu_physical_cores indicates SMT.

gpu_id.description: Device UUID where available, otherwise the device index as a string.

nstep.description: Number of measurement-phase timesteps requested for this sample.

measurement_profile.description: DYNAMICS_ONLY and PRODUCTION_LIGHT results must not be mixed in one crossover curve without explicit labelling.

timing_method.description: How process_wall_seconds was obtained. EXTERNAL_PROCESS_WALL_CLOCK is the harness measuring the complete executable; INTERNAL_REPORTED is a timer reported by UppASD itself.

process_wall_seconds.description: Complete process wall time: startup, input parsing, allocation, Hamiltonian/neighbour setup, GPU init, FFT planning, simulation, requested measurements and finalization. null only when the run produced no valid timing.

setup_seconds.description: Reserved derived field. Fitted fixed-cost intercept of T(n) = T_fixed + n*t_step; it is an intercept, not a directly measured pure setup cost. Always null in a raw sample record -- it is filled in by aggregate/fit records.

steady_step_seconds.description: Reserved derived field. Fitted steady-state production timestep. Always null in a raw sample record -- it is filled in by aggregate/fit records.

numerical_valid.description: The run completed and produced physically/numerically acceptable output. Independent of environment quality.

environment_valid.description: The measurement environment was suitable for authoritative timing evidence. A run that completes correctly on a busy GPU is numerically valid but not environment valid.

allOf.$comment: CPU runs carry no GPU identity or GPU precision.
Every GPU run names its programming model, whether or not it executed. HIP is representable here even where no HIP hardware exists.
A GPU run that actually executed must identify the device and its software stack. A skipped or failed GPU run legitimately has no device metadata.
Neighbour-list workloads must carry neighbour-workload metadata.
FFT/dipole workloads must carry explicit grid metadata.
Pure neighbour-list workloads carry no FFT grid.
MIXED precision is deliberately not implemented in production; it is representable as an unsupported state rather than as a failed build.
An unsupported precision mode cannot be claimed numerically valid and cannot enter a precision comparison.
PRECISION_MATCHED requires an audited, supported precision mode.
A GPU record may only claim PRECISION_MATCHED when the audited CPU and GPU numerical paths genuinely agree. CPU double against GPU single is PRODUCTION_CONFIGURATION.
Environment validity is the conjunction: any raised quality flag clears it. Flagged samples remain usable as developer evidence, but not as authoritative timing.
A completed run must carry a real measured process wall time.
A run that did not complete is not numerically valid and is not authoritative timing evidence.
Derived timing fields are reserved and stay empty in raw sample records.
A clean tree lists no dirty files.
A dirty tree must raise the dirty_tree quality flag, which in turn clears environment_valid.
